notes: Initial ontology. Skills are grouped by domain. Transfer weights are directional: source → target. A weight of 1.0 means full transfer (rare); 0.7 means strong transfer; 0.4–0.6 means moderate. All weights are subject to evidence-based review.

aware.definition: Understands the concept and has studied or experimented with the skill; has not applied it in a real-world or production context.
aware.ui_prompt: I understand the concepts and have tried this in a personal or learning context, but have not used it professionally.
criteria: Completed a course, tutorial, or self-directed study on this skill
Can explain core concepts accurately to someone unfamiliar with the area
Has written code or produced work using this skill, but it was never shipped or relied on by others
aware.llm_classification_hint: Candidate mentions the skill by name or in an education context but shows no applied or professional usage. Phrases like 'studied', 'familiar with', or 'learning' without shipped examples indicate Aware.
aware.job_brief_guidance: Candidate will need active mentoring to apply this skill. Do not list as a must-have unless you are prepared to invest significantly in training.

practitioner.definition: Applies the skill to deliver real outcomes in a professional or open-source context; does so with occasional reference to documentation or guidance from more senior colleagues.
practitioner.ui_prompt: I have used this in a real job, project, or open-source contribution. I get things done with it, sometimes looking things up.
criteria: Used this skill in a paid, volunteer, or open-source role to complete real work tasks
Has shipped or contributed to work that others relied on, even once
Completes standard tasks independently; looks things up or asks for help on complex problems
practitioner.llm_classification_hint: Candidate describes using the skill to complete work tasks or projects. May mention needing help from more senior colleagues on complex problems. Evidence of shipped work is the key signal.
practitioner.job_brief_guidance: Can contribute independently on standard tasks. Needs support for complex or novel scenarios. A realistic entry-level must-have for most roles.

proficient.definition: Applies the skill reliably and independently across a range of real-world scenarios; can debug non-trivial problems and actively supports others.
proficient.ui_prompt: I work independently with this skill across varied situations. I debug hard problems and often help teammates.
criteria: Owned a feature, system, or area of work end-to-end in a professional context
Resolved complex or production issues without escalation
Regularly reviews colleagues' work in this area or is a go-to person for questions
proficient.llm_classification_hint: Candidate shows ownership, deep problem-solving, or mentoring/reviewing others in this skill area. Look for 'led', 'owned', 'designed', 'resolved' language paired with concrete outcomes.
proficient.job_brief_guidance: Solid independent contributor. Handles most scenarios without escalation. Safe must-have baseline for most mid-level and above roles.

expert.definition: Deep mastery; designs or shapes how the skill is applied across a team or system; understands internals, edge cases, and failure modes at a level others in the organisation do not.
expert.ui_prompt: I understand this deeply — internals, failure modes, trade-offs. I have shaped how it is used in an organisation or project, built tooling for others, or spoken or written about it publicly.
criteria: Designed architecture, standards, or patterns that others in an organisation follow
Authored libraries, tooling, or internal frameworks used by other practitioners
Diagnosed deep or systemic issues that others could not resolve
Has presented, written, or published on this topic for a technical audience
expert.llm_classification_hint: Candidate shows impact at a system or team level: architecture decisions, tools built for others, public talks or writing, or deep diagnostic work on issues others could not solve.
expert.job_brief_guidance: Can define technical direction and resolve issues others cannot. Reserve for roles where this depth is genuinely required — avoid defaulting to Expert as a must-have for standard roles.

authority.definition: Recognised beyond their organisation as a leading practitioner; shapes the discipline through standards, research, open-source stewardship, or community leadership.
authority.ui_prompt: I am a recognised leader in this area beyond my organisation — through open-source stewardship, published research, standards work, or community leadership.
criteria: Maintains a widely-used open-source project with external production users or significant community
Published research, specifications, or standards in this area
Invited speaker at major industry conferences on this topic
Co-authored a widely-adopted standard, specification, or framework
authority.llm_classification_hint: Candidate has clear external recognition: widely-used OSS stewardship, peer-reviewed publications, standards authorship, or keynote-level conference speaking. Very rare — do not infer from seniority alone.
authority.job_brief_guidance: Rare. Only require this for roles where external credibility and discipline leadership are a genuine, stated part of the job. Most senior roles do not require Authority.

C# and Java share OOP paradigm, similar type systems, and ecosystem patterns.
